title: Whether a provider url passed for one call may choose a private address, in three languages
pins: Whether a provider url passed for ONE call (`using(provider, model, {url})`) is refused before any request when it names a loopback, private, link-local, shared, unique-local, unspecified or cloud metadata address, written as a literal in the spellings an OS resolver reads (IPv6 forms that carry an IPv4 address included), or named by a stock hosts file, and whether a host is judged exactly as written: an escape, any character a hostname or address literal may not hold, or a format, invisible or IDNA deviation character, is refused rather than decoded or converted. A per-call url is chosen by whoever builds the call, so a url that reaches 169.254.169.254 or a service behind the firewall in one language and is refused in another is an SSRF hole in whichever accepts it, and nothing errors to say so. Configured urls are the operator's and are deliberately not checked; they appear only as controls, together with the one explicit configuration opt-out and the proof that the call itself cannot turn it on.
scope: The openai provider and one named openai-compatible entry, entered through Prism.text().using() in each language. Address literals in decimal, octal, hex, shortened, IPv6, IPv4-mapped, NAT64, SIIT IPv4-translated and ISATAP spellings, the RHEL, openSUSE, Debian and macOS hosts-file names and names under localhost.localdomain, userinfo in front of the host, local and metadata names with case and trailing-dot variation, percent escapes in names, address literals and IPv6 literals, characters no host may hold, a backslash in the authority, zero-width joiners, other invisible characters and the IDNA deviation characters, an empty written host, a public name with a trailing dot and a public international name, one non-http scheme, and the configuration controls. NOT covered: a public hostname that RESOLVES to a private address (no language resolves names here, by design: the check makes no network call), DNS rebinding, the reference's other providers and custom providers (each language's own regression tests cover those), and the refusal message, which is outside the contract.
construction: Native PHP manager entered through Prism::text()->using() with Laravel's HTTP fake and stray requests prevented, reading the package's own config/prism.php against each row's environment; native TypeScript Prism.text().using() with fetch captured; native Python Prism.text().using() with the default transport's send captured and DNS and sockets refused. Every fixture answers 500, because only whether a request went out matters. Each observation is `dispatched` and the refusal code, and nothing else: tools/per-call-url-guard/contract.mjs refuses any other field and any row both dispatched and refused.
findings: 77 of 77 rows agree on the fix branches (prism, prism-ts and prism-py `fix/g365-per-call-guard-gaps`). Against the code before that fix, 77 of 77 ALSO agree, and 14 of the 22 new rows agree because all three languages SENT the request: the RHEL, openSUSE, Debian and macOS hosts-file names, a name under localhost.localdomain, SIIT IPv4-translated and ISATAP addresses carrying loopback or the metadata address, and public names holding a sharp s or a final sigma. Agreement could not see any of them. The zero-width joiner rows record no refusal code in any language, because each language's clean-url check refuses them before the guard runs; the guard on its own refuses them too, which each language's unit rows assert, since this suite only enters through using(). Earlier: on the code before the as-written host rule, 43 of the first 55 rows agreed, and PHP sent 9 of its 19 hostile rows, TypeScript 3 and Python 10. Agreement here is a conclusion about behaviour, not about safety: the three guards follow one spec, so a shared misreading of it would agree here too. A hostname that resolves to a private address is not refused, in any language, because no language resolves names here. A few malformed hosts that one language's URL parser rejects before the address step still report scheme_not_allowed where another reports private_address_refused (a non-ASCII host that IDNA maps to `%`, for example); no row exercises that case, and every such outcome refuses before any request.

discrimination.gap: No mutation probe is delivered for this suite. Three coarse negative controls: the code before the per-call guard fails 29 to 30 of the first 34 rows in every language; the code before the as-written host rule fails 12 of the first 55; and the code before the G-365 fix sends 14 of the 22 rows added with it, in all three languages, while every row still agrees.

php.note: Run the corpus-loading entry point with php --check. PRISM_PHP_SRC points it at a prism checkout (CI uses the default branch); without it, it reads the installed reference in runners/php.

ts.note: Run the corpus-loading entry point with ts --check; it reads the built sibling prism-ts/dist, or PRISM_TS_DIST.

py.note: Run the corpus-loading entry point with py --check; it imports the installed package, or PRISM_PY_SRC.
